findings.title: Negative one is pluralised: -1 formats as "-1 Bytes" while 1 formats as "1 Byte"
findings.function: humansize::ISizeFormatter::fmt (the body behind FormatSizeI::format_size_i; the impl_style feature is not enabled in the harness so the wrapper itself could not be called)
findings.property: formatting -v is the same as formatting v with a leading '-' (singular/plural unit choice depends only on magnitude)
findings.evidence: formatters.rs says 'Remove "s" from the scale if the size is 1.x' but the check f64_eq(ipart, 1.0) uses the signed integer part, so it never fires for -1.x. Same for -1 kB-scale values, e.g. -1000 long decimal gives "-1 Kilobytes" vs "1 Kilobyte". Negation symmetry is the natural contract of format_size_i, whose docs show 1_000_000 -> "1 MB" and -1_000_000 -> "-1 MB".

error.message:
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: "-1 Bytes"
 right: "-1 Byte"

review.title: Singular unit not chosen for negative sizes with magnitude 1.x (-1 formats as "-1 Bytes")
review.reason: The code comment says the "s" is removed when the size is 1.x, and the rest of ISizeFormatter works on magnitude (fabs for scale selection and integer-part rendering). The plural check `f64_eq(ipart, 1.0)` uses the signed `modf` integer part, so it never fires for negative values. The result is that 1 gives "1 Byte" and -1 gives "-1 Bytes", which is an unintended asymmetry. The fix is a one-line `fabs(ipart)`, and no test or doc requires "-1 Bytes". The only doubt is that "-1 bytes" is arguably acceptable English, and the effect is limited to long units and bit-scale 0 with negative inputs.

fix.reason: the repro passes on the patched code
